## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment Product
where: ReportService (uses), src/business/reportService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const name = this.products.findById(t.productId)?.name ?? t.productId;
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are two different concepts. In ReportService (node a663bd12cbc0090c, src/business/reportService.ts), the line `const name = this.products.findById(t.productId)?.name ?? t.productId;` shows that a treatment `t` points to a product through `productId`, and the product's name is fetched from ProductRepository. So A is the Product: something that exists in a catalog and has its own name. B is the treatment itself. TreatmentRepository (node b2566037ba6b6900, src/persistence/repositories.ts) stores `TreatmentRecord[]`, and each record is one application of a treatment to a hive (it is looked up via findByHive). A treatment refers to a product, so the two are linked but are not the same thing. They are kept in separate repositories, ProductRepository and TreatmentRepository.
